messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pagerduty alert triggered for routing-service-high-latency (P-2345). Significant uptick in cross-region tail latency from eu-west-1 -> us-east-1, spike started ~5187654300. Investigate.

pagerduty: Paging alex (oncall) and mia (sre). Escalation level 1.

alex (oncall): I saw the page, jumping on it. Is anyone already digging into routing-policy changes?

mia (sre): I pulled topology traces — ~7% of requests originating in eu-west-1 are getting steered to us-east-1 unexpectedly. Latency shows from ~60ms -> 320ms tail. Errors 502 spike to ~1.8%.

jon (netops): On it. I'm seeing a flurry of routing-policy commits around 5187654287 from the routing-controller. There's a commit that toggled "region_pin_heuristic" to "enabled" briefly then rolled back. But DNS pins appear to have uneven propagation.

linda (eng-runtime): Runtime telemetry shows a mismatch between route evaluation and what the control-plane thought was active. Rule id rp-9943 shows two active variants for a 30s window. Could be a race during canary flip.

alex (oncall): Mia — any customer-facing impact yet? Sarah from support, can you confirm?

sarah (support): We're getting multiple tickets about slow responses and a few timedout webhooks. Customers in EU complaining of higher latencies and occasional 502s. No major data loss, but user-visible errors.

mia (sre): Agreed. Severity: P2 (partial customer impact across region). Mitigation plan: 1) Disable region_pin_heuristic in control plane (safest rollback), 2) Force flush short TTL CNAME caches for affected edge pools, 3) Re-run policy dry-run and confirm single-source-of-truth.

alex (oncall): I can disable heuristic. Linda, can runtime accept a graceful policy revoke? We should avoid mid-flight KV cache poison.

linda (eng-runtime): Yes — we have a safe revoke endpoint: POST /control/policy/revoke?grace=true. It drains new evaluations but doesn't kill active KV. It will take ~30s to propagate.

jon (netops): I'm ready to also push a targeted BGP announcement to prefer eu-egress for the affected prefix to reduce routing variance while we fix policy. That will take ~60s to converge.

alex (oncall): Ok, execute steps in parallel. I'll initiate revoke now.

alex (oncall): `curl -X POST "https://control.redwood-inference.internal/control/policy/revoke?grace=true" -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx"`

linda (eng-runtime): Received revoke request, returning 202. Propagating to evaluation agents. Estimated full propagation 35s.

jon (netops): Initiating targeted BGP preference for eu-egress (asn 64532) on the regional fabric. Command shown below:

```
# netops command (runbook snippet)
route-map PREFER_EU permit 10
 set local-preference 200
exit
apply route-map PREFER_EU to neighbor 203.0.113.10
```

jon (netops): Done — waiting for convergence.

mia (sre): Observability: within 90s tail latency dropped from 320ms -> 85ms. Error rate steadily returning to baseline.

alex (oncall): Nice. Sarah, please escalate to the support triage and update the customer-facing status page: "Investigating increased latency for EU customers; mitigation in progress." Add note that some webhooks may have timed out.

sarah (support): Will do. Update posted.

linda (eng-runtime): Control-plane logs for commit rp-9943: shows two nearly-simultaneous canary flips (commit ids c-1184 and c-1185) with conflicting pins. When the operator rolled back c-1185, some proxy agents had already cached pins with TTL 60s. Combined with downstream DNS resolution TTLs, a minority of flows persisted to wrong region.

mia (sre): Root cause hypothesis: race in routing-controller's canary rollout path + short TTL pin caching in edge proxies. Fix: add serialized commit application (leader lock) and make proxies respect a short-lived soft-lease on pins instead of full TTL.

alex (oncall): For immediate next steps: 1) Keep region_pin_heuristic disabled (control plane), 2) Netops to keep BGP preference for 10 min then ramp down, 3) Runtime to publish patch to respect soft-lease and ignore pins if commit mismatches (hotfix PR), 4) Postmortem and customer comms owner assigned.

jon (netops): Will keep BGP change for 10m and then monitor.

linda (eng-runtime): Working on a hotfix branch: `hotfix/ignore-stale-pins`. Patch will add verification of commit-id on proxies. PR will be ready in ~40m; can be canaried to a single pool first.

mia (sre): I'll schedule a post-incident eval: metric set includes geo-tail-latency, cross-region-rate, pinned-flow-count, and policy-commit-conflicts. Need thresholds for automated rollback next time.

sarah (support): Customers updated on status page and notified top 10 customers via email templates. Monitoring for incoming tickets.

alex (oncall): Any objections to closing pager? Impact reduced and we have active mitigations. If anything regresses we can reopen.

mia (sre): Close pager now, continue monitoring in channel for 2 hours. We'll open a formal incident doc later.

incident-bot: Pager P-2345 marked resolved by alex (oncall) at 5187654418.

alex (oncall): Thanks team. Follow-ups: action items in the incident doc: enforce serialized policy commits, change proxy pin lifetime semantics, add pre-commit policy dry-run gating for canary flips, and run a geo-traffic chaos test. I'll assign owners in the postmortem.

sarah (support): Filing summary for customers and marking impacted tickets with incident tag.

mia (sre): Adding action item: add an alert that triggers if >2% cross-region flow increase in any 5m window to catch similar regressions faster.

jon (netops): I'll run a quick BGP rollback in 10m and provide a small playbook snippet for future use.

alex (oncall): Closing thread for now. Will re-open if regression. Thanks. :thumbsup:
